stages.title: Engine Gap — L2.4 Checkout Trace Bus-Publish
stages.notes:
Phase A: Fix the ONE material deviation. L2.4 checkout trace cannot follow bus-publish ServiceLink edges because Type nodes (BasketCheckoutEvent) have no edge to their containing Service node. Fix: extend OutEdgesWithTwin() in TraceBuilder.cs and SelectBestSpineEdge() in GraphBuilder.cs to bridge Type->Service when node.Project is known. Flip [TruthPending("L2")], verify depth >= 5, verify checkout flow traces across 3 services.

PRIOR SESSION FINDING (session 1, commit 4d997d9): Bridge code IS written in OutEdgesWithTwin() (TraceBuilder.cs:440-454) and SelectBestSpineEdge() (GraphBuilder.cs:239-257). Build 0w/0e, tests 518P/3S, truth 8P/3S — no regressions. BUT the bridge cannot activate because the Raises edge from BusPublishDetector is NOT created on the real dogfood repo. The BusPublishDetector passes unit tests (SeamDetectorTests.Use) but fails on real dogfood analysis — likely a TypeDiscovery or SourceBody pipeline issue where the handler type isn't correctly discovered for real analysis vs the synthetic test.

DO NOT rewrite the bridge code — it's correct. Investigate why BusPublishDetector doesn't create the Raises edge: trace BodyFactExtractor pipeline for the CheckoutBasketCommandHandler in the dogfood repo (eShop). Check if AddSeamsFromDetectors → BodyFactExtractor pipeline processes the handler type. Compare: what does the unit test's synthetic CheckoutHandler do differently from the real one? The test may use in-memory types while analysis uses file-derived types — SourceBody may differ.

Read docs/design-reviews/R1-L0-L3.md:62-66 for the full enforcement attempt story. Read docs/workflows/loom-gap-close-plan.md Phase A for deep root cause analysis.
